Checkpoint 41 — LAN onboarding portal + download counter

Checkpoint 41 — LAN onboarding portal + download counter

What landed

The "LAN Connection Approval Gate": a captive-style onboarding portal inside the control panel binary, reachable pre-approval, with a live served-download counter and two enrollment scripts. Soft-portal flow only — gateway enforcement is a designed follow-up (contract documented, not implemented), per the architecture decision: master laptop hosts the onboarding AP + portal, the separate cluster router carries all cluster traffic.

Counting semantics (the part that must not be misunderstood)

  • requests = every hit of a script endpoint (HEAD, Range: bytes=0- resume probes, 304 revalidations, aborted transfers).
  • downloads = full 200 GET with the entire body written. A retry cannot inflate it; a browser preview doesn't count; a successful download counts as both (requests include downloads).
  • Neither number proves the user saved or executed the file. The portal page states this verbatim; so does docs/lan-onboarding-portal.md.
  • Unique devices = distinct sha256(salt‖IP‖UA) per artifact; unique_devices = union across artifacts. IP/UA are spoofable and documented as directional; MACs are not used; raw values are never stored or served.

Why the scripts live in internal/portal/assets (not repo root)

go:embed needs a compile-time-stable path, and a root copy would drift from the served one. join-cluster.sh (the legacy gatekeeper) stays untouched at the root; joining-cluster.sh is the new portal enrollment agent and has a different job: register → poll approval → switch Wi-Fi → (Hosts, optional) k3s agent install with a confirm prompt.

Proofs

  • gofmt clean; go build ./... OK; go vet OK; go test -count=1 ./... green (all packages; join 10s).
  • bash -n joining-cluster.sh clean; --detect-only exercised with Host (12/16/nvidia), Guest (4/8/none), boundary RAM=15 → Guest, and the real machine.
  • test-joining.sh: 5/5 pass.
  • npm run build: tsc + vite clean, dist rebuilt with the two new metric tiles.
  • Portal routes verified through the router test suite: page wins over the SPA fallback, /portal/ variant works, count/stats behave, stats requires JWT.
  • Live end-to-end (panel binary + real script + real approval):
    • Portal page, script download (correct Content-Type + Content-Disposition: attachment), HEAD + Range probes counted as requests only (requests=4, downloads=2 after 2 GETs + HEAD + 0-20 probe), public count aggregate-only, stats 401 unauthenticated / full detail with JWT, downloads.json persisted with salt + one hashed device.
    • Approval path: script registered (32-char ID), instructor approved via POST /api/nodes/{id}/approve, script observed approval within one poll cadence, printed the Wi-Fi manual step, exit 0.
    • Denial path (TEST_HOSTNAME override → fresh fingerprint): script reported DENIED by the instructor: laptop does not qualify, exit 1.
    • JOIN_KEY path: panel with JOIN_KEY → script without the key → join key rejected immediately.
    • Idempotency: two consecutive script runs registered the same node id (server-side fingerprint dedupe), node count stayed 1.

Bugs the E2E caught (fixed in the same checkpoint)

  1. NODE_ID="" POLL_BODY="" PANEL_URL="" clobbered the user's PANEL_URL env var before main() ran — discovery fell through to the prompt every time. Globals line removed.
  2. log() output inside register/wait_approval was captured by command substitution (body=$(...)), so diagnostics vanished and poll bodies got polluted with log lines. Both functions now hand results back via REG_BODY/POLL_BODY globals and log to stdout.
  3. The poll used curl -f, so the approved-node 503 join service unavailable (no minter outside the cluster / K3S_JOIN_URL unset) was swallowed as a transport failure — approval was never observed. The poll now parses every response; those two 503 bodies are recognized as "approved, token not mintable yet" and the flow proceeds with a clear caveat. The same 503 semantics are documented in control-panel/README.md (pre-existing behavior).
  4. The "Registered as node …" line hardcoded pending; it now reports the server's actual status (matters on re-registration of approved/denied nodes).
  5. Added TEST_HOSTNAME override (alongside TEST_* hardware overrides) so a second laptop's fingerprint — and therefore the deny path — is testable on one machine.

Not done here (deliberate)

  • Gateway/firewall enforcement: contract only (GET /api/gateway/devices sketch in the design doc). Enforcement stays at the gateway/router; approval state and enforcement remain decoupled so any router integration bolts on without touching the core.
  • Redirect/interception of arbitrary client HTTP: soft portal by design; the AP's dnsmasq wildcard-DNS trick (documented) covers most browser attempts.
  • Node records don't store MAC/last-IP yet — needed only when a gateway integration lands; the design doc notes where they'd go.
